## Problem

A vendor supplying GenAI components makes claims the review cannot
take at
face value — model provenance, training-data posture, subprocessor
list, incident history. The review frameworks are REAL
and published (ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act's obligations).
But **Kailash ships no governance template pack** — the pre-#210 D-6
rows (the governance template-pack family) were phantom-origin
template packs (no real upstream anywhere) and the os#210 audit
removed them
([os#210](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210); the
four names ride the registry there). The task: run the review NOW,
honestly, with the framework documents as the checklist source.

## Solution

Work from the upstreams directly — the frameworks are public. The
review is the lab's document discipline, not tooling:

```bash
# 1. Get the vendor's OWN declarations in writing:
#      model/system card, training-data summary, subprocessors,
#      incident/notice history, data-retention terms
# 2. Map each claim to the framework requirements you are auditing
#    against (read requirement text from the published standard —
#    ISO/IEC 42001: AI Management System; NIST AI RMF 1.0 functions
#    GOV/MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE; EU AI Act high-risk obligations per annex)
# 3. For every claim the vendor cannot evidence: that is your finding
#    list; tier findings by risk and own the follow-up
# 4. Record your review as a dated, versioned document (this book's
#    no-invented-evidence rule, applied to governance): claim + source +
#    date per row; never write "verified" where you read a claim
# 5. When the D-6 template packs rebuild (the
#    os#210 rebuild contract — built pack first, verified upstream,
#    then the manifest gate), this recipe re-opens with the real
#    pack interfaces.
```

What success looks like:

- every review row names its framework clause + the vendor's evidence
  (or its absence — also evidence)
- the four citation components: framework + clause, vendor artefact,
  reviewer, date
- nothing in the review claims compliance — reviews FIND, auditors
  attest

## Discussion

- **Why no pack exists yet:** building a checklist pack for AI Act /
  AI RMF / 42001 review is exactly the work the registry's
  rebuild contract covers — the names are parked, not deleted
  ([os#210](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210)).
- **The framework texts are the checklist source of truth:** read
  them from the published upstreams; a template pack (when one is
  built) renders views of THEM, never replaces them.
- **Pair the review with the technical evidence chain:**
  [Evidence for a standards-mapped control statement](standards-evidence.html)
  produces tool-run-backed evidence that the governance findings can
  cite — regulation asks for control evidence; the lab's runs provide
  it.
